method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Occurs in heavy users** (daily or almost daily over months) after abrupt cessation or a large reduction. It may not be the presenting complaint — it can arise during any admission.
claims.source_text: Cannabis withdrawal syndrome (CWS) is a well-characterised phenomenon which occurs in heavy cannabis-users (daily or almost daily use over months) after abrupt cessation or significant reductions in cannabis use … Cannabis withdrawal may not be the presenting complaint and can occur in the context of any young person's admission
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Time course:** starts 1–2 days after last use, peaks on days 2–6, usually settles in 2–3 weeks; sleep disturbance may persist for months.
claims.source_text: CWS typically occurs 1-2 days after last use. The acute phase symptoms peak at day 2-6. Symptoms usually subside after 2-3 weeks but some symptoms eg sleep disturbance may persist for months
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common features:** irritability, insomnia, anxiety, low mood, aggression, decreased appetite, nausea, headache.
claims.source_text: Common features of cannabis withdrawal Irritability Insomnia Anxiety Low mood Aggression Decreased appetite Nausea Headache
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Predictors of severe withdrawal:** previous complex withdrawal (aggression, suicidal ideation or attempt, psychosis) · polysubstance dependence · co-occurring mental health or medical conditions (e.g. T1DM, IBD).
claims.source_text: Factors associated with severe withdrawal Previous complex withdrawal eg aggression, suicidal ideation or attempt, or psychosis Polysubstance dependence Co-occurring mental health disorders or medical conditions (eg T1DM, IBD)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nicotine co-dependence is common** (cannabis is often mixed with tobacco), and **withdrawal from both is more severe.**
claims.source_text: Most dependent cannabis users have concurrent dependence to nicotine due to the common practice of mixing cannabis with tobacco. Withdrawal from both nicotine and cannabis can lead to more severe withdrawal symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Distinguish cannabis hyperemesis syndrome** — recurrent severe nausea from regular use, not withdrawal — managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, dopamine antagonists and topical capsaicin cream.
claims.source_text: Cannabis hyperemesis syndrome is a condition characterised by recurrent, severe nausea. It is associated with regular cannabinoid use rather than being a withdrawal syndrome. It should be differentiated from CWS and managed with IV fluid hydration, antiemetics, dopamine antagonists and topical capsaicin cream
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine vital signs, look for intoxication or withdrawal, and do a mental state examination.** The Cannabis Withdrawal Assessment Scale helps grade severity but **is not validated for guiding medication.**
claims.source_text: Vital signs Physical exam to identify signs of intoxication/withdrawal Mental state examination … The Cannabis Withdrawal Assessment Scale can assist with assessment of the nature and severity of cannabis withdrawal. However, it is not validated for the use of medications in response to symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer opportunistic sexual health, pregnancy and blood-borne virus screening**, and catch-up vaccines (hepatitis B, HPV; consider hepatitis A).
claims.source_text: Opportunistic sexual health, pregnancy and blood-borne viruses screen … Opportunistic vaccinations should be offered if not up to date, including Hepatitis B and HPV (consider hepatitis A)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urine drug screens should not be routinely performed** — cannabinoids can persist in urine for several weeks.
claims.source_text: Urine drug screens should not be routinely performed Note: cannabinoids can persist in the urine for several weeks after cessation of use
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Management is supportive and non-pharmacological for the vast majority; there is no standard medication regimen** — only short-term PRN symptom relief.
claims.source_text: Management is supportive and non-pharmacological for the vast majority. There is no standard medication regimen for cannabis withdrawal. Rather, short-term PRN medications are prescribed for symptom management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Psychoeducation** on symptoms, onset, duration and coping; **cravings** — the 3 D's (delay, distract, deep breathing), urge surfing, mindfulness, and check HALTs (hunger, anger, loneliness, tiredness).
claims.source_text: Educate young person and their carers regarding common withdrawal symptoms, their likely onset, duration and coping strategies … The 3 D’s (delay, distract, deep breathing) Urge surfing Mindfulness strategies Consider other common causes of cravings (HALTs: Hunger, Anger, Loneliness, Tiredness)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep the environment quiet, calm, safe and private**; encourage small regular light meals and hydration to avoid dehydration.
claims.source_text: Minimise stress by ensuring that the environment is quiet, calm, safe and private … Recommend the young person try to maintain small regular light meals over the course of the withdrawal episode, and to maintain hydration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pain/headache:** paracetamol 15 mg/kg (max 1 g) qid prn; ibuprofen 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg) tds prn; hyoscine butylbromide for abdominal cramps.
claims.source_text: Pain/headaches Paracetamol 15 mg/kg (max 1 g) qid prn Ibuprofen 10 mg/kg (max 400 mg) tds prn Hyoscine butylbromide for abdominal cramps
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nausea and vomiting:** ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg (max 8 mg) orally tds prn; cyclizine 1 mg/kg (max 50 mg) 8-hourly orally/IV/IM; metoclopramide 10 mg tds prn — ⚠️ **risk of extrapyramidal effects with metoclopramide.**
claims.source_text: Nausea and vomiting Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg (max 8 mg) orally tds prn Cyclizine 1 mg/kg (max 50 mg) 8 hourly orally/IV/IM Metoclopramide 10 mg tds prn Caution: risk of EPSE with metoclopramide use
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe withdrawal/agitation:** diazepam 5 mg orally qid prn (**max 20 mg in 24 hours**); higher doses only under appropriate supervision; **senior clinician review; wean over 5–7 days.**
claims.source_text: Severe withdrawal/agitation Diazepam 5 mg orally qid prn (max 20 mg in 24 hours) Higher doses of diazepam may be required for some young people, use with appropriate clinical supervision Senior clinician review Wean over 5-7 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not prescribe benzodiazepines in the outpatient setting without specialist consultation.**
claims.source_text: There are risks involved in introducing young people to benzodiazepines, hence caution must be used in prescribing them. They should not be prescribed in the outpatient setting without specialist consultation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe withdrawal not responding to diazepam:** olanzapine 2.5–5 mg orally bd prn — **diazepam first; seek specialist advice.**
claims.source_text: Severe withdrawal not responding to diazepam Olanzapine 2.5-5 mg orally bd prn Use diazepam before using olanzapine Seek specialist advice
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Insomnia:** melatonin 2–5 mg orally nocte.
claims.source_text: Insomnia Melatonin 2-5 mg oral nocte
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Concurrent nicotine dependence:** nicotine replacement — **a long-acting patch plus a short-acting form is most effective**; doses per AMH Children's Dosing Companion.
claims.source_text: Nicotine withdrawal (if concurrent nicotine dependence) Nicotine replacement therapy Combination of long-acting (patch) + short-acting (lozenge, inhaler, gum, spray) is most effective Refer to AMH Children’s Dosing on nicotine replacement therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** for severe or complex withdrawal (polysubstance use, mental illness, other comorbidities), help choosing the treatment setting or titrating sedatives, or safety concerns.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Withdrawal is more severe or complex due to polysubstance use, concurrence of mental ill-health, physical, neurodevelopmental and/or psychosocial co-morbidities Needing assistance in determining appropriate treatment context for young person (outpatient, inpatient, drug and alcohol unit, mental health unit) Needing assistance in titrating sedating medications Concerns about young person’s safety due to drug and alcohol use
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer if tertiary mental health care is needed.** **Discharge with a clear follow-up plan covering drug and alcohol and psychosocial needs**, and link to post-withdrawal services (associated with better outcomes).
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Young person requires tertiary-level mental health care … Consider discharge when Clear plan for follow-up is in place which address drug and alcohol as well as psychosocial concerns … Linking the young person with relevant voluntary services post-withdrawal is associated with improved outcomes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cannabis withdrawal syndrome' (Last updated December 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cannabis_withdrawal_syndrome/, retrieved 2026-09-23
